experiment: Stage 2.5 score-only ordering plus structural exact TT
hypothesis: Adding the already-validated structural exact transposition table to score-only ordered search further reduces expanded nodes and may recover enough work to offset cache overhead without changing any action.
interpretation: Action equivalence held at every tested frozen position for depths 2, 3, and 4.
At depth 2 there were no transposition hits, so the combined engine changed no node counts and remained slower than both baseline and score-only ordering.

At depth 3 the structural TT reduced the score-ordered engine from 2409 to 2097 expanded nodes, an additional 12.95 percent reduction, for a total 44.47 percent reduction relative to Baseline A. Wall-clock time was 1.3 percent slower than score-only ordering and 66.1 percent slower than baseline.

At depth 4 the structural TT reduced the score-ordered engine from 9349 to 7203 expanded nodes, an additional 22.95 percent reduction, for a total 56.83 percent reduction relative to Baseline A. It was 4.3 percent faster than score-only ordering, though still 12.1 percent slower than baseline.

Transposition caching therefore continues to recover meaningful duplicate work even after alpha-beta move ordering changes the traversal. The remaining performance bottleneck is the cost of computing the ordering estimate itself, not a lack of pruning opportunity.

The next isolated hypothesis should preserve the score-only ordering policy exactly while computing its sibling ordering score incrementally from the parent state rather than recomputing full child score breakdowns.
